note: Twenty commits from BestPractice's own history, before the Precedent work began, chosen for a spread of change kinds: prose-only edits, tool changes, template additions, engine work, and lifecycle records. Each is a moment where a session was about to do real work and some subset of the catalogue genuinely applied. c01-c10 were the v1 pilot; c11-c20 widen it.

cases.task: Clarify the README: it should capture intention and thinking rather than reading as a document-editing tool.
Fix phrasing in the install documentation that implied approving a change isn't real work.
Correct INSTALL.md: the approval moment is the review-and-merge, not step 7.
Add a baseline .gitignore, installed at the repo root, covering tool and interpreter caches.
Make checkin.py's freshness check emit an automated upstream staleness notice, while taking the update stays a deliberate human act.
Fix a bug: record() must advance synced_from, or push() false-positives on the next cycle.
Add VOICE.md and STYLEGUIDE.md templates and wire them into the install prompt.
Record that GitAround has moved out into its own repository.
Enforce practice 33's rule 2 by adding a restatement check to doc_sync.
Clarify practice 16: the date on a volatile rule is the contributor's, not the agent's system clock.
Add a Claude Code Stop hook that blocks ending a turn with unpushed work.
Recover three pre-gate content losses found by a historical scan of the repository.
Add the carry-all-pending rule, restore the erased blocks, and add the mechanical gate for it.
Close two audits: verify the wiring registry, and add an opt-in unsourced-quantity gate.
Guard both directions of the checkin mirror, and record why in practice 14.
Check in practices 24-25 from a dependent repo, plus the bootstrap apt-retry pattern.
Check-in: update tooling, harden the lint, and add a repo-wide renumber rule.
Add practices for named check levels and for a merge-authorization keyword.
Add practice 30: scripts assert their own properties and their sources' figures.
Add practice 33: documents track their models, and every transformation is code.
